name: Titirangi / Kaiti Hill
bio: A hill with a lookout over the bay and the site of Cook's first landing, a good spot for sunrise.

name: Tolaga Bay Wharf
bio: The longest wharf in the Southern Hemisphere, at 660 metres, with a nearby cave walk.

name: Gisborne Wine Centre
bio: A wine bar and tasting room on the inner harbour that stocks local Chardonnay.

name: Wainui Beach
bio: A long golden surf beach east of the city, popular with surfers and walkers.

name: Tairāwhiti Museum
bio: A regional museum of Māori and early European history beside the river, with Cook's landing artefacts.

name: East Cape Lighthouse
bio: The easternmost lighthouse in New Zealand, reached by a steep stairway, one of the first places to see the sunrise.

name: Hicks Bay
bio: A sheltered bay on the north coast with a wharf and a quiet beach.

name: Te Araroa Pōhutukawa
bio: Te Waha o Rerekohu, a huge pōhutukawa tree thought to be the largest in the country, beside the school.

name: Tokomaru Bay
bio: A small bay with an old wharf, a quiet beach and views of the coastline.

name: Cooks Cove Walkway
bio: A coastal walk to a cave through the rock at Cooks Cove, with views of Tolaga Bay.
